surprises: BLOCKING x ARMED, found by this cell and remediated in it: AllowAdvisorRouterOAIPlatinumAdvi was LIVE on opal-data-portal-v2 and managed by NO terraform resource. aws_s3_bucket_policy is FULL-REPLACE, so ANY shared-infra apply by anyone for any reason would have deleted a live serving grant and 403'd the ADVI route that went live at ~15:57Z the same day. Plan-proven before any apply (0 add / 1 change / 0 destroy, the change being the REMOVAL of that Sid). Disarm: a fabric-wide shared-infra apply freeze, owner AE, carried by MSTR. Remediation: codified in the same edit as the etfs ARN, one apply, re-plan 0-diff in the owning root. Freeze lifted 65786; independently verified by COO (65790), CVO and CTO. HOW IT HID: the grant was applied on the live primitive and verified on the live primitive during P4R-3 -- sound for 'is it granted', structurally silent on 'does code still describe reality' -- and the re-plan that read 'No changes' ran in portal-auth, which does not own the bucket policy. THE VERIFICATION RAN IN THE WRONG TERRAFORM ROOT. Generalisable: a live-primitive grant with no corresponding terraform resource is a deletion scheduled for whenever someone next applies that root.

MY OWN FALSE CLAIM, self-caught and corrected same-turn before any apply: I asserted 'public-data-router is DYNAMIC/qualified_arn [OK], the edit takes effect on apply, no version pin blocks it', citing comp-routes edge-versions. FALSE. lambda-edge.tf:197 carries ignore_changes = [qualified_arn, source_code_hash]; the apply would have published a new version while CloudFront kept serving the old one, with a clean plan, a genuine 0-diff re-plan, a really-published version and the route green on old code. The file warning against exactly this -- 'Do not read that [OK] as evidence an edge moved' -- was written the SAME DAY, by MY OWN LANE, in the very file I was editing. Contract went to v1.1 with the correction on its face; the mint became three edits. CVO confirmed the misreport is LIVE (the tool marks all five [OK] including the three pinned) and added the sharper limb: comp-routes' own coverage disclosure cross-references the reader TO edge-versions for the pinning axis -- it routes you to the instrument that gets it wrong.
